newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens, swaps up on spillover.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens, swaps up on spillover.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in moderate early trading on Thursday and swap rates edged up on renewed spillover from Thailand.
One local bank dealer said the rupiah declined on ample supply and on short dollar covering ahead of the weekend.
Overnight rupiah was traded at 10.0 percent. Short-term swaps were soft, with overnight swaps trading at 0.25/0.30 and tom/next at 0.85/0.90 points. But spot/next firmed at 0.3/0.4.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.1/29.5 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.75/28.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,428.3/28.7 and 2,428.0/28.4, respectively.

The local bank dealer said operators were cashing out from previous short dollar positions, lifting the rupiah toward the resistance level at 2,430. However, some dealers said the dollar remained heavy at the 2,430 level.

Fears of a swap squeeze like in Thailand continued to hang over the Jakarta forward market, especially after Thailand's Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan confirmed on Thursday that he planned to resign from his post.
The embattled minister is expected to submit his resignation letter to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh later on Thursday, his aides said.
Dealers said swap premiums increased on uncertainty in Thailand and intervention by the Philippines central bank.
They said it was unlikely Bank Indonesia would implement such a measure. However, offshore investors remained uncomfortable.
One-month swaps edged up to 13.75/14.25 from 13.25/14.00, two to 27.5/29.5 from 26.0/28.0 points while three-month was at 41.0/42.0 and six at 81.0/82.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,422/2,614 and its conversion band at 2,422/2,470 on Wednesday.
